details:
ORBITAL ENGINEER – Project Details

ORBITAL ENGINEER is an interactive, educational spacecraft design and mission simulation game that places players in the role of a spacecraft engineer. The project aims to make the engineering behind real-world space exploration accessible through hands-on gameplay, problem-solving and resource management.

How the Game Works

Players design and assemble spacecraft by selecting components from an engineering inventory and integrating them into a functional spacecraft. The component catalogue covers multiple spacecraft subsystems, including structural bodies, power generation and storage, propulsion, communication, navigation, attitude control, scientific instruments and mission-specific equipment.

Each component has engineering attributes such as mass, power consumption or generation, cost, and functionality. Players must balance these factors while meeting mission requirements and available resource budgets. Components can be moved, added and removed during assembly, with connections between structural, power and data systems. The game also incorporates compatibility checks and design validation to identify invalid connections and engineering constraints before a mission can proceed.

Missions and Progression

The game features a historical campaign inspired by five major space missions: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), Cassini–Huygens, Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity), Juno and Dawn.

An important aspect is historical accuracy. Each historical stage enforces technology restrictions appropriate to its mission and launch era, requiring players to work with equipment that would have been available at that time.

After spacecraft construction and validation. The gameplay uses simplified, deterministic engineering calculations to demonstrate design trade-offs rather than attempting to replicate a full professional spacecraft simulator.

Benefits, Creativity and Intended Impact

ORBITAL ENGINEER combines gaming with STEM education, transforming abstract concepts such as power budgets, spacecraft mass, propulsion, communication and system compatibility into practical decisions. The combination of component-based construction, resource management, historical technology limitations and progressive experimentation makes learning interactive rather than purely theoretical.

The project is designed to encourage curiosity about aerospace engineering, improve systems-thinking and problem-solving skills, and introduce players to the multidisciplinary decisions involved in designing spacecraft.

Tools and Development

The game is developed as a browser-based web application using HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript. Its interface follows a retro pixel-art aesthetic inspired by spacecraft control systems, with a dark navy and teal colour palette, technical panels and space-themed visual elements. AI-assisted development tools were used to support implementation, content preparation and visual asset creation.

Throughout development, the team considered technical accuracy, component compatibility, historical feasibility, gameplay balance, accessibility, usability and educational value. Particular attention was given to distinguishing real mission hardware from simplified gameplay representations and estimated component statistics.

Ultimately, ORBITAL ENGINEER aims to turn the complexity of spacecraft engineering into an engaging experience where players can design, experiment, learn and explore.
